items.title: Next.js: Cache leak across root param values in nested 'use cache' functions via delayed inner stream metadata
items.text: With Cache Components enabled, an outer `'use cache'` function can be keyed incorrectly even when its inner `'use cache'` call generates a fresh entry. If the inner function reads a root param (via `next/root-params`) and returns a value that still contains pending promises — for example an object with data that is ready immediately alongside slower data — React Flight delivers the ready portion to the outer function before the inner entry has finished publishing its root param dependencies. The outer function can then finish, and its cache entry is persisted under a key that omits that root param. The entry is written once and reused for all root param values, so a response for one root param value can serve content produced for a different value. Entries written this way can also ignore tag invalidation and cache lifetimes of the nested caches they consumed. What values are leaked cannot be attacker controlled. Which value's content is served depends only on which invocation wrote the entry first. This is a variant of https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h694-7cp9-m8p3 that the fix for that advisory does not cover: it does not require the inner call to be served from an existing en

items.title: Standard builds move to usage-based billing for new teams
items.text: Starting today, new Pro and Enterprise teams no longer include a Standard build slot. This brings Standard builds under the same usage-based billing model as other build machines. On Pro, Standard builds cost $0.014 per build minute, and your monthly usage credit applies to build usage. Enterprise rates follow your contract. Standard builds remain billable after switching from Elastic to Standard for teams covered by this change. items.title: Speed Insights now measures soft navigations
items.text: now measures soft navigations: client-side route changes that update page content without a full reload. This means you can now track performance as users move through your app, not just on full-page loads.Speed Insights Speed Insights captures LCP, FCP, INP, and CLS for soft navigations and includes these measurements in your Real Experience Score. TTFB is not captured because there is no new document request. Soft-navigation tracking is enabled by default for all projects using Speed Insights, with no action required. It works with modern web frameworks such as Next.js, SvelteKit, and Nuxt, in Chromium-based browsers. In your project's , use the new filter to view , , or navigation data. items.title: Optimizely Supply Chain Attack Distributes Malware Across Global Brands
items.text: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform on November 16, 2026, distributing malicious JavaScript through websites operated by some of the world's largest brands. Security researcher Scott Helme of Report URI identified 188 infected JavaScript snippets associated with 178 organizations, including the BBC, CNN, Zoom, GitLab, IKEA, and HSBC. The attack exposed website visitors to malware designed to replace cryptocurrency wallet addresses, steal payment information, and deliver iOS exploit kits. Optimizely Web Experimentation is used for A/B testing and website personalization. Organizations using the service embed JavaScript snippets from Optimizely's content delivery network into their websites. These snippets include an optional Project JavaScript field that allows custom code to execute across pages. The attacker inserted malicious code into that field, which was then served through Optimizely's trusted infrastructure. The affected organizations did not need to have their own websites or servers compromised for the malicious scripts to reach visitors. items.title: Microsoft’s agent-framework PyPI package Compromised with Credential Stealer
items.text: Executive Summary # The Microsoft agent-framework PyPI package was compromised on November 17th, affecting versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2. Both versions install Python startup hooks that silently collect credentials, environment data, and cloud identity tokens, then exfiltrate them to a webhook[.]site endpoint. Avoid installing either version; if installed, remove them and rotate potentially exposed credentials. Attack Analysis # On Python startup, the .pth file imports a module that launches collection in a background process/thread. Version 1.26.1 routes through agent_framework_meta.pth → agent_framework_meta/**init**.py → agent_framework_meta/_telemetry.py; 1.26.2 uses af_runtime_diag.pth → af_runtime_diag.py. The code gathers credential-related environment variables, local config/credential files, and other processes’ environments. It also requests cloud/workflow identity tokens (including Azure in both versions and GitHub Actions OIDC in 1.26.2). It serializes the results, compresses and Base64-encodes them, then POSTs them to the same concealed webhook.site endpoint: https[://]webhook[.]site/d381fd80-ec62-42ad-8f5c-d1b15103c9bb Version 1.26.1: startup hook → package initializer →
